blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — ACE-inhibitor fetal toxicity and medication safety action
stem: A client taking lisinopril reports a newly confirmed pregnancy. Which nursing action is most appropriate?

options.A: Continue lisinopril through the first trimester and review therapy later because the most recognized fetal renal toxicity occurs in the second and third trimesters.
options.B: Contact the prescriber promptly; current labeling directs discontinuation of lisinopril as soon as pregnancy is detected because of fetal toxicity risk.
options.C: Reduce the lisinopril dose and continue treatment until an obstetric visit because lower exposure avoids the fetal toxicity described in current labeling.
options.D: Continue the current regimen if blood pressure is controlled and arrange routine prenatal follow-up because stable maternal pressure prevents medication-related fetal effects.

rationale: The current lisinopril boxed warning and Warnings and Precautions §5.1 state that when pregnancy is detected, lisinopril should be discontinued as soon as possible because drugs acting directly on the renin-angiotensin system can cause fetal injury and death. Therefore the nurse should promptly contact the prescriber so therapy can be changed in accordance with the warning. A is incorrect because the labeling does not support continuing through the first trimester despite the particularly recognized second- and third-trimester fetal renal toxicity. C is incorrect because dose reduction is not presented as a way to remove fetal toxicity risk. D is incorrect because controlled maternal blood pressure does not prevent medication-related fetal toxicity.
educational_objective: Respond promptly when pregnancy is detected during lisinopril therapy because current labeling directs discontinuation as soon as pregnancy is detected due to fetal toxicity risk from renin-angiotensin-system drugs.
source_organization: DailyMed (U.S. National Library of Medicine); packager: RemedyRepack Inc.
source_locator: Boxed Warning — Fetal Toxicity and Warnings and Precautions §5.1 Fetal Toxicity: when pregnancy is detected, discontinue lisinopril as soon as possible; drugs that act directly on the renin-angiotensin system can cause injury and death to the developing fetus.
source_claim_supported: Pregnancy detected during lisinopril therapy requires prompt medication review because current labeling directs discontinuation as soon as pregnancy is detected due to fetal toxicity risk.
blueprint_locator: Printed p. 38, Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies: educate client about medications; review pertinent data prior to medication administration; evaluate client response to medication.
candidate_reasons_resolved: Rewrote all four options to comparable length and parallel clinical-action structure.
The correct option is no longer uniquely longest, and each distractor remains plausible but directly contradicted by current labeling.
audit_note: Clinical content was re-audited from zero after revision. B matches the boxed warning and §5.1. A incorrectly delays action, C invents a dose-reduction safety strategy, and D confuses blood-pressure control with elimination of drug-specific fetal toxicity. No second defensible answer remains and the original length cue is resolved.
